`feat`: **Add plugin-registrable action system (RFC #1380)** ([#1404](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/ShokoServer/pull/1404)):

* feat(abstractions): add plugin-registrable action system

Implemented the RFC from discussion #1380 (v7): plugins and core can now register discrete, invokable actions that are listed through the API, filtered by scope and caller permission, and always executed through the job queue.

- Added `IExecutableAction` with a required `Name`/`Permission`, an optional `Validate` pre-check, a `RequiresConfirmation` UI hint, and `SeriesAction`/`GroupAction`/`EpisodeAction` base classes with an internal `IScopedAction` context setter, plus `IActionCaller` for caller identity.
- Added the `ActionService` registry with load-time validation, UUIDv5 action IDs namespaced by plugin ID, and `ActionExecutionJob` as the single queue-backed execution wrapper.
- Added the listing and invoke endpoints: `GET /api/v3/Action?scope=`, `POST /api/v3/Action/{actionId}`, and `POST /api/v3/{Group|Series|Episode}/{id}/Action/{actionId}`.
- Ported 60 existing actions from `ActionController` and the scoped controllers to the new shape, including bucket-1 variant pairs and bucket-2 open-ended property sets; the legacy endpoints remain available but are marked obsolete.
- Registered core actions transient in DI and plugin actions via `PluginManager`; added `InternalsVisibleTo` to `Shoko.Abstractions` so the load-time `IScopedAction` guard is enforceable.

* feat(abstractions): expose action listing and invocation to plugins

Added the plugin-facing contract so plugins can enumerate registered actions and invoke them programmatically, not just through the HTTP API.

- Added `IActionService` to `Shoko.Abstractions` with `GetActions`/`GetActionInfo` listing and typed `InvokeAsync` overloads for global, series, group, and episode scopes.
- Moved `ExecutableActionInfo` into `Shoko.Abstractions` without the concrete action type so the plugin-facing surface never leaks server internals; the server keeps the type in a private registry entry.
- Invocations now validate that the action's scope matches the supplied entity, require a caller for `IActionCaller` actions, and skip the permission gate for trusted programmatic calls without a caller.
- Dropped the separate core action registrations (the DI sweep in `SystemService` and the extra core `AddParts` call in `PluginManager`): the plugin manager already discovers core action types, since the core is registered as a plugin like any other.

* docs(actions): fix unresolved XML doc references

Replaced a `<paramref>` on a type-level remark and an unresolvable `ActionService` cref with plain text, so `Shoko.Abstractions` builds with zero warnings.

* fix(actions): harden caller resolution and category name fallback

`ActionExecutionJob` now only resolves the calling user when a caller was recorded, so trusted programmatic invocations never fail with a missing-user error. `ActionService.AddParts` marks the assembly-name fallback for `PluginInferred` categories as non-null.

* feat(actions): support bucket-2 invocation parameters

`IActionService.InvokeAsync` gained parameter-accepting overloads for all four scopes, `ActionExecutionJob` carries a `Parameters` payload through `JobDataJson`, and the job populates the matching public settable properties of the action instance before executing — the Gap 23 bucket-2 mechanism for programmatic invocation.

* fix(actions): return 404 for unknown action IDs on scoped routes

The series/group/episode invoke routes now check for an unregistered action ID and return a clean 404, matching the global route instead of surfacing an unhandled `KeyNotFoundException`.

* fix(actions): include parameters in dedup key and validate against them

Made `Parameters` a `[JobKeyMember]`, so invoking the same action on the same scope and caller with different parameters enqueues instead of silently collapsing into an already-queued job. Also moved parameter population into a shared helper and applied it to the probe instance before `Validate()`, so validation observes the caller-supplied values rather than compiled-in defaults.

* docs(actions): reword planning and migration-scoped comments

Dropped the "Gap N" planning-doc references and the "matches today" temporal parity notes left in code, per review. The surrounding prose was kept and reworded to state the what/why directly: permission comments now describe the legacy endpoints admin gate as a permanent invariant, and the execution comments describe the transient lifetime, queue-only execution, and bare-ack contract without the numbered spec tokens. Also fixed the stale `IScopedAction` guard framing and a missing word in `IExecutableAction` docs.

* chore(actions): remove legacy parity comments from action permissions

Removed the per-action comments noting whether the legacy endpoint was
admin-gated. The `ActionPermission` value is self-documenting and the
migration parity rationale does not belong in the shipped code.

`fix` (`tmdb`): **Add season-scoped nearest-air-date fallback for episode linking** ([#1389](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/ShokoServer/pull/1389)):

* fix(tmdb): add season-scoped nearest-air-date fallback for episode linking

`TryFindAnidbAndTmdbMatch` previously fell straight from the strict
±2-day `TryAirDateMatch` window to a blind positional `FirstAvailable`
guess, which mismatched delayed/compressed episodes onto the wrong
TMDB slot (e.g. AniDB episode 2 grabbing episode 5's TMDB entry).

- Added `TryNearestAirDateMatch`, tagged with a new
  `MatchRating.NearestDateMatches` (distinct from the strict-window
  `DateMatches`), using the unbounded `CalculateAirDateDistance` to
  pick the closest remaining candidate by air date instead of by list
  position, bounded by `MaxFallbackDifferenceInDays` (120) so it can't
  confidently link episodes separated by an unrelated multi-month gap.
- Scoped the fallback candidate pool to `anchorSeasonNumber`, resolved
  from whichever neighboring AniDB episode already has a confirmed
  TMDB link (via an incrementally maintained `Ordering == 0` primary-
  link dictionary, not a linear scan), so a back-to-back multi-cour
  release (e.g. season 1 ending in March, season 2 starting in June)
  can't have this pull an unresolved episode across the season
  boundary. When neighbors disagree on season, the closer one by air
  date wins instead of always preferring the previous episode.
- `ResolveRankedMatch`'s cache-reuse now also invalidates when a
  same-pass neighbor resolves a new anchor mid-pass, not just when the
  cached TMDB candidate gets claimed.
- `CalculateAirDateProbability` now delegates to
  `CalculateAirDateDistance` instead of duplicating the day-diff math.

* chore(tmdb): remove redundant null-forgiving operators in TmdbLinkingService

Nullable warnings are disabled for this file, so the `!` operators were
pure noise; addressed the SonarCloud S8970 findings and cleaned up the
remaining instances in the same file while in there.

* fix(tmdb): mark TryAirDateMatch/TryAnyTitleMatch crossRef out params as NotNullWhen(true)

* refactor(tmdb): extract episode-matching local functions to class members

Pulled ResolveAnchorSeason/RankByConfidence/ResolveRankedMatch out of
MatchAnidbToTmdbEpisodes into proper private methods, per review
feedback on #1389. Added EpisodeMatchContext to carry the shared state
(GetEpisodeList kept as a delegate since FilterToCurrentSeasons mutates
the episode lists between passes) instead of duplicating a growing
parameter list across the three. Also restored IsSpecialEpisode as a
shared helper instead of the inline expression getting duplicated at
both new call sites.

* refactor(abstractions): rename NearestDateMatches to DateKindaMatches

Matches the existing *KindaMatches naming convention (TitleKindaMatches,
DateAndTitleKindaMatches) per harshithmohan's review.

* fix(tmdb): annotate nullable out params on title/air-date match helpers

TryTitleMatch (shared by TryExactTitleMatch/TryKindaTitleMatch) and
TryNearestAirDateMatch assigned `null` to a non-nullable `out
CrossRef_AniDB_TMDB_Episode` parameter, producing CS8625 warnings.
Sibling methods TryAirDateMatch/TryAnyTitleMatch already used
`[NotNullWhen(true)] out CrossRef_AniDB_TMDB_Episode?` for the same
pattern; applied it consistently here too.

* fix(tmdb): address code review findings on episode date-matching

- `anidbEpisodesByTypeNumber` now built with GroupBy+First instead of
  `ToDictionary`, which threw on any duplicate (EpisodeType,
  EpisodeNumber) pair — the only other accessor for this exact lookup,
  `AniDB_EpisodeRepository.GetByAnimeIDAndEpisodeTypeNumber`, already
  treats that as non-unique.
- The loose (±120 day) `TryNearestAirDateMatch` fallback is now gated
  by `isSpecial`, matching the positional `FirstAvailable` fallback
  below it — a special with no title match could previously be
  auto-linked to whatever TMDB episode was nearest in air date up to
  four months away, with zero corroborating evidence.
- Collapsed the two copies of the special-episode predicate (a closure
  in `MatchAnidbToTmdbEpisodes` and a static method used by
  `RankByConfidence`/`ResolveRankedMatch`) into one shared
  `IsSpecialEpisode(EpisodeType, AnimeType)` helper.
- Rewrote the `nearestAirdate` LINQ chain as a query expression so the
  `distance is not null` filter is visible to nullable analysis across
  the following `select`, clearing a CS8629 warning.
- Wrapped the new/changed method signatures in this diff that exceeded
  the repo's 160-character line limit.

* test(tmdb): cover the isSpecial gate on the loose air-date fallback

Adds SelectBestEpisodeMatch_DoesNotUseLooseAirDateFallback_ForSpecials
and its _ForNonSpecials counterpart, guarding the previous commit's fix
where a special with no title match could get auto-linked purely on
air-date proximity up to 120 days away.

`fix` (`workflows`): **Don't fail nuget publish when release tag already exists** ([#1405](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/ShokoServer/pull/1405)):

The daily build republishes packages whose version wasn't bumped since
the last successful run. dotnet nuget push --skip-duplicate already
tolerates this for the package itself, but rickstaa/action-create-tag
was still hard-failing every Publish *Nuget job on reruns because the
git tag from the prior publish already exists.

`fix` (`workflows`): **Force-push the release tag on nuget publish** ([#1406](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/ShokoServer/pull/1406)):

#1405's tag_exists_error: false never took effect: action-create-tag's
existence check is git tag -l, a local check, but the daily-build
runner does a fresh checkout with no tags fetched — it always sees
'not exists' locally and tries to create+push the tag fresh, which the
remote then rejects since the tag is already there. force_push_tag
force-pushes unconditionally, which is a no-op when the tag already
points at the same commit.

`fix` (`db`): **Add missing primary keys on SQL Server for 38 tables**:

SQLite and MySQL both declare PRIMARY KEY on these tables' identity
columns; the SQL Server migration file never did, leaving them as
heaps. Confirmed live via sys.dm_db_missing_index_details on a
production instance — TMDB_Episode_Cast and TMDB_Episode alone
accounted for the two highest-impact missing-index findings, forcing
RID lookups instead of clustered-key seeks on every query.

Adds migration 180: ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT PRIMARY KEY
CLUSTERED for all 38 affected tables. Dry-run tested in a rolled-back
transaction against a live production database with no conflicts.

`fix` (`api`): **Surface series whose only candidate has ambiguous per-episode coverage**:

`VideoReleaseGroupingService.Group()` correctly collapses files that agree
on group/version/location into a single candidate, but `MightHaveMultipleCandidates`,
`ComputeCandidates`, and the `Series` list endpoint all required more than
one candidate before a series would surface in Release Management. That
hid series whose files merge into one candidate but still leave an episode
covered by more than one file with nothing to distinguish them (an
untagged v2) — observed live with `Sousou no Frieren (2026)`, whose
episodes 9 and 10 each had 2 files from the same release and never
appeared at all.

`MightHaveMultipleCandidates` now flags any episode covered by two
distinct video files regardless of version/location agreement, and the
new `HasAmbiguousEpisodeCoverage` lets `ComputeCandidates` keep a
single-candidate series when that candidate has such an episode, so
`ReleaseCandidate.EpisodeCoverage`'s `PlaceIDs` can do what it was built
for. Removed the now-unused `VideoLocal_PlaceRepository` dependency from
the grouping service.

`feat` (`api`): **Show variations that fit an existing release candidate**:

Variations (`VideoLocal.IsVariation`) were previously excluded wholesale
from `ReleaseManagementController`'s candidate grouping unless
`includeVariations=true`, even when a variation covered the same episode
as a file already shown in a candidate. That's the same "two valid files
for one episode" situation as a multi-part release, just caused by an
unmarked re-release rather than an intentional split — it should be
visible the same way.

`VideoReleaseGroupingService.GetFileDisplaySignals` computes a single
video's quality signals and episode coverage outside the grouping
pipeline (factored out of `BuildSignature` via a shared `ComputeQualityCalc`
helper so the two paths can't drift). `ReleaseManagementController` uses it
to build `ReleaseCandidate.DisplayOnlyFile` entries for a series' variation
videos; `ReleaseCandidate.FromCandidate` attaches one to a candidate only
when its episode coverage overlaps that candidate's own, tagged via the new
`File.IsVariation` flag. A variation matching none of a series' candidates
stays hidden, same as today, unless `includeVariations=true`.

This is deliberately display-only: variations attached this way are always
`IsRedundant = false` and never enter `ComputeCandidates`'s
grouping/redundancy pipeline, so `Preview`/`Execute` deletion and the
background auto-management job are unaffected — they already ignore
variations unconditionally.

`feat` (`api`): **Expose PlaceIDs per episode on ReleaseCandidate**:

When a single release candidate has multiple files covering the same
episode (a multi-part release, or the grouper's "ambiguous" full-collision
case such as an untagged v2), `EpisodeCoverage` previously gave no way for
a client to tell there was more than one file without cross-referencing
every `File.Episodes` list. `PlaceIDs` now lists every `File.PlaceID` that
covers each episode, so a client can show all included files instead of
only surfacing one.

`feat` (`buildtools`): **Add shoko-build CLI tool for plugin builds**:

Introduces Shoko.BuildTools, a dotnet tool that wraps MSBuild with
assembly metadata injection, source-level auto-tag discovery, manifest
management, and release packaging.

- Injects PackageID/Name/Overview, dependencies, tags, runtime
  identifier, and git metadata into the built DLL as assembly metadata
- Auto-discovers Shoko service interface implementations (IReleaseInfoProvider,
  IHostedService, etc.) using Roslyn syntax trees and prepends them as tags
- Manages manifest.json: creates/updates release entries with download
  URLs and SHA256 checksums, with per-channel pruning support
- Packs build output into a .zip archive
- Supports multi-RID builds (reads RuntimeIdentifiers from the project)
- Template substitution for {runtime}, {version}, {name}, {abstraction}
  in --url and --output arguments
- Auto-detects manifest.json in CWD, project directory, or parent
- Publishes to NuGet as a global tool (shoko-build)

Server-side changes:
- PluginManager reads embedded PackageID/Name/Overview and dependencies
  from assembly metadata, preferring them over IPlugin instantiation
- Warning logged when embedded metadata is missing
- Embedded identity used in failure fallback paths (legacy namespace,
  ABI mismatch, missing dependencies) instead of generated stubs
- Error messages const-ified for reuse

Closes workflow integration with daily and release pipelines.

`feat` (`api`): **Add plugin dependency resolution and lifecycle enforcement**:

Introduces a full plugin dependency system across the server, API, and
SignalR layers.

Data models:
- PluginDependency type (PluginID, VersionRange, IsOptional) in
  Shoko.Abstractions
- Dependencies lists on LocalPluginInfo, PackageReleaseInfo, and
  RemotePackageReleaseInfo
- RemotePackageDependencyInfo for manifest JSON deserialization

Resolution service:
- IPluginDependencyResolver interface with ResolveDependencies,
  GetDependents, GetUninstallCascade, ValidateEnable/Disable methods
- PluginDependencyResolver implementation with version range parsing
  (>=, ^, ~, exact), transitive cascade traversal, and cycle detection

Lifecycle enforcement (PluginController):
- Enable blocked by missing dependencies (412 Precondition Failed)
- Disable blocked by dependents (409 Conflict) unless Force=true
- Uninstall shows cascade and requires force=true

Install integration (PluginPackageController):
- autoResolveDependencies query parameter on install endpoint
- Missing dependencies return 424 Failed Dependency unless auto
  resolving

API endpoints:
- GET /api/v3/Plugin/{id}/Dependencies — resolved dependency tree
- GET /api/v3/Plugin/{id}/Dependents — reverse dependency list
- GET /api/v3/Plugin/DependencyGraph — full graph

SignalR:
- PluginEventEmitter broadcasts plugin:installed / plugin:uninstalled
  events via AggregateHub

`fix` (`db`): **Make NHibernateDependencyInjector's type-info caches thread-safe**:

`Instantiate()` runs concurrently across NHibernate sessions on different
worker threads. Its two static type-info caches (`s_allTypes`,
`s_typeHasValidConstructors`) were plain `Dictionary`s with an
unsynchronized check-then-add pattern:

    if (!s_typeHasValidConstructors.TryGetValue(clazz, out var hasParameters))
    {
        hasParameters = ...;
        s_typeHasValidConstructors.Add(clazz, hasParameters);
    }

Two threads racing on the same not-yet-cached `clazz` both miss the
`TryGetValue` and both call `.Add()` concurrently, corrupting the
dictionary's internal state (`InvalidOperationException: Operations
that change non-concurrent collections must have exclusive access`).
The corruption is permanent for the process's lifetime — every
subsequent `Instantiate()` call touching that dictionary throws until
the process restarts, cascading into any code path that instantiates
an NHibernate entity (observed via TMDB metadata jobs and the Lua
renamer's `Studios` access).

The race window only opens right after a restart, before the caches
warm up, which is why this went unnoticed since it was introduced in
2023 (`4e720796f`) — it needs concurrent first-time access to the same
entity type in that narrow window, which a startup job backlog makes
far more likely than steady-state traffic.

Swapped both caches to `ConcurrentDictionary`.
